newsitem.title: USA: Utah sues tobacco companies to recoup Medicaid fees.
newsitem.headline: Utah sues tobacco companies to recoup Medicaid fees.

text.p: Utah, in a bid to recoup the cost of state Medicaid funds spent on tobacco-related disease, on Monday sued a group of tobacco companies, a state spokesman said.
Utah joins 15 other states and a number of cities and counties that have filed lawsuits against the tobacco giants.
"We sued to recoup Medicaid costs, but also to put a hold on the targeting of youth," said Todd Utzinger, a spokesman for Utah Attorney General Jan Graham.
While the state did not specify a dollar figure in its lawsuit, Utzinger said that tobacco-related costs to Medicaid in Utah from 1993 until the present stood at $128 million.

Michael York, spokesman for Philip Morris Cos. Inc., one of the companies sued, said he had not seen the suit but believed it would be a "copy cat, cookie cutter lawsuit" based on earlier state cases.
"So far we not seen any cases with any legal merit and we and we don't expect to," York said.
